channel.title: Board of Project Stewardship News
channel.description: Local construction news from the Board of Project Stewardship for King County, Snohomish County, and Seattle.

item.title: Edmonds extends landmark tree limits while it finishes a permanent tree code
item.description: The Edmonds City Council voted unanimously Oct. 13 to extend its interim landmark-tree rule for up to six more months and adopted an interim process for short plat vacations.

item.title: Seattle opens Environmentally Critical Areas code update with October listening sessions
item.description: SDCI is making its first major update to Seattle's Environmentally Critical Areas code since 2017 and will hold four online listening sessions Oct. 22-29 before drafting changes.

item.title: Seattle breaks ground on Mount Baker affordable housing and early learning campus
item.description: Partners broke ground Oct. 15 on a 3.8-acre Mount Baker Redevelopment near Link light rail, with more than 400 planned affordable homes and the Rainier Rising Early Learning Campus.

item.title: Snohomish County Council votes to let homeowners split residential lots without a council hearing
item.description: The Snohomish County Council unanimously approved Ordinance 26-036, moving two-lot residential splits to an administrative review by the county's planning department.

item.title: Snohomish County Health Department wins $70,000 state grant to speed septic reviews for new homes
item.description: A state Commerce grant will help the Snohomish County Health Department link its septic review software with county planning, so reviews for new homes can start sooner.
